facts.fact: ITWeb Africa reports that the regulator INCM validated the Internet Para Todas e Todos (Internet for All) national strategy, a roadmap to 95% broadband coverage by 2030 (period 2026 to 2030), presented in Maputo on 2026-10-08, without stating adoption by the government or a minister.

facts.fact: The Bureau de Conteudo Local, republishing Noticiaslusofonas, reports that INCM is presenting and validating a proposed National Strategy Internet para Todos with government, operators and partners, setting targets to 2030; the date of the session is not stated, so the publication date 2026-10-08 is used.

Lusa via Club of Mozambique reports that a proposed Internet for All strategy, implemented by INCM with targets through 2030, was presented in Maputo; the presentation date is not given, so the publication date 2026-10-07 is used.

note: A digest of GSMA 5G figures; it names no national broadband plan or strategy for Mozambique.

facts.fact: Wearetech.africa reports that the Internet Para Todos programme, launched in March 2025, targets 80% mobile penetration, 95% territorial coverage and 99% network availability by 2030, a period that had not ended.

note: Describes a phased 5G rollout with 2027 and 2030 coverage targets; it names no national broadband plan, so it is an operator/spectrum rollout (other), not a plan fact.
A presidential 5G pledge and a universal-coverage-by-2030 aim; names no national broadband plan or strategy by name, so no plan fact.

facts.fact: The U.S. International Trade Administration reports that the government is drafting a Digital Transformation Strategy covering connectivity, e-government and social services (note dated 2025-07-16, which is also the as_of date).

The U.S. International Trade Administration reports that in December 2024 the government launched the Internet for All project, aiming to raise internet access from under 25% to 100% of the population by 2030, with a period running to 2030.
